findings.title: Embedded-post author color changed in light theme
findings.body: The topic-map embedded-post author link was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)), so the light-theme branch is no longer the previous value and the dark branch is the complement of 70%, not of 30%. Light-theme author names in expanded replies become much lighter, and dark theme does not get the muted color this change is supposed to produce.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness not preserved
findings.body: Topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). It is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Desktop keeps 20% for light and 80% for dark. On mobile, light-theme headings jump from a near-primary 20% to a mid gray, and dark theme is not the complement of the original 20%.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message-length colors are swapped
findings.body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new rule is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). Desktop correctly keeps 70% in the light branch and 30% in the dark branch. Mobile inverts both, so light-theme hint text gets darker and dark-theme hint text gets much lighter than the rest of this change.

findings.title: Group member name color collapsed to title color
findings.body: .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), distinct from .title at 50%. Both are now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Light theme loses that distinction, and the dark-theme name color is not the complement of the original 30%.

findings.title: Mobile group member name color also rewritten
findings.body: Same mistake as desktop user styles: .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), matching .title. Light-theme names change shade, and dark theme does not use the complement of 30%.
